summary:
This back-matter page holds two quick-reference tables reproduced from the book.

**Loss, last-layer activation, and metrics to use for different tasks (chapter 6)**

| Task | Last-layer activation | Loss function | Metrics |
|---|---|---|---|
| Binary classification | Sigmoid | Binary crossentropy | Binary accuracy, ROC AUC |
| Multiclass, single-label classification | Softmax | Categorical crossentropy | Categorical accuracy, Top-k categorical accuracy, ROC AUC |
| Multiclass, multi-label classification | Sigmoid | Binary crossentropy | Binary accuracy, ROC AUC |
| Regression | None | Mean squared error | Mean absolute error |

**Model architecture for different data types (chapter 20)**

| Input | Output | Model |
|---|---|---|
| Vector data | Class probability, regression value | Densely connected network |
| Timeseries | Class probability, regression value | RNN, Transformer |
| Images | Class probability, regression value | ConvNet |
| Text | Class probability, regression value | Transformer |
| Text, images | Text | Transformer |
| Text, images | Images | VAE, diffusion model |

The first table matches the output layer to the loss: sigmoid outputs pair with binary crossentropy (one independent probability per label), softmax outputs pair with categorical crossentropy (one distribution over mutually exclusive classes), and regression uses a linear output with MSE. The second table is the architecture summary from chapter 20's "Key network architectures" (PDF 624–629).

concepts.name: Last-layer activation and loss pairing
concepts.definition: The output activation and the loss must match the task: sigmoid + binary crossentropy, softmax + categorical crossentropy, no activation + MSE.
concepts.intuition: The output layer has to produce the kind of quantity the loss expects: a probability per label, a probability distribution over classes, or an unbounded number.
concepts.technical: Multi-label classification uses sigmoid, not softmax, because the labels are not mutually exclusive.
concepts.significance: Getting this pairing wrong is one of the most common beginner bugs.
concepts.example: Tagging a photo with any number of {cat, outdoor, night}: 3 sigmoid units + binary crossentropy.
concepts.misconception: Softmax is not right for multi-label problems: it forces the probabilities to sum to 1.

misconceptions.claim: Multiclass multi-label classification should use softmax.
misconceptions.correction: The table gives sigmoid + binary crossentropy, because each label is an independent yes/no decision.
The table says 'None': a linear output so the model can predict any real value.

earlier.note: Choosing the loss function in chapter 6 (index: 'loss function 181'); likely location of the first table's material.
Chapter 20 'Key network architectures' (printed 600), the source of the second table.

takeaways: Binary and multi-label classification: sigmoid + binary crossentropy.
Regression: no activation + MSE, monitored with MAE.
Architecture follows data type: dense for vectors, ConvNets for images, Transformers for text, VAEs/diffusion for generating images.

questions.question: Which last-layer activation and loss does the table give for multiclass, multi-label classification?
questions.explanation: Labels are not mutually exclusive, so each gets an independent sigmoid probability and binary crossentropy. Softmax + categorical crossentropy is for single-label; None + MSE is regression; softmax + binary crossentropy is a mismatch.

questions.question: Which metric does the table recommend for regression?
questions.explanation: The regression row uses MSE as loss and MAE as metric.

questions.question: Which model families does the table list for generating images from text and images?
questions.explanation: Last row of the architecture table.

questions.question: Why is softmax wrong for a multi-label problem?
questions.answer: Softmax makes the outputs sum to 1, so labels compete; in multi-label problems several labels can be true at once.
questions.explanation: Sigmoid gives an independent probability per label, which is what the table recommends.
